summary: Creates a department of health education and outreach program on reproductive health services for consumers, patients, educators, and health care providers related to reproductive health services available in New York state including, but not limited to: access to family planning services such as contraceptives and pregnancy testing, testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections; makes related provisions.
title: Creates a department of health education and outreach program on reproductive health services

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 41
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Assembly Bill Number 778-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to directing the
      department  of health to create an informational pamphlet concern-
      ing intrauterine devices"
 
Assembly Bill Number 2168, entitled:
 
    "An ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring the
      department of health to develop and maternal health care providers
      to distribute written information about  episiotomy  to  maternity
      patients"
 
Assembly Bill Number 2581-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the creation
      of a  women's  and  reproductive  health  services  education  and
      outreach program"
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 1720, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing
      an awareness campaign on the use of hormone replacement therapy in
      treating the symptoms of perimenopause and menopause"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  These four bills would require the Department of Health to develop and
distribute written materials, create an education and outreach  program,
and  establish an awareness campaign on specific public health topics. I
share a strong interest in these topics and commend the Legislature  for
addressing them.
 
  However,  enactment of this package of legislation would impose a cost
to the Department that is not accounted for in the State Financial Plan.
Without appropriate funding, these unbudgeted costs would create signif-
icant  staffing  and  other  programmatic  burdens  on  the  Department.
Because of the fiscal impact of this legislation, the proposals would be
more  appropriately  considered in the context of the State budget proc-
ess.
 
  Furthermore, the Department, as well as numerous clinical and  profes-
sional  organizations, already provide ample evidence-based and patient-
centered guidance and information related to the  public  health  topics
mentioned in these bills. Such guidance and information is accessible to
health care providers and the general public.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto these bills.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
